title: UAE becomes first country worldwide to approve new use of Ultomiris for immune-mediated kidney disease
summary: Emirates Drug Establishment reinforces its regulatory leadership in approving innovative therapies and expanding treatment options for patients

Dr Ruqaya Aqeel Al Bastaki, Acting Executive Director of the Medical Products Regulation Sector at the Emirates Drug Establishment. Image Courtesy: Emirates Drug Establishment

Emirates Drug Establishment reinforces its regulatory leadership in approving innovative therapies and expanding treatment options for patients

Press Release

Dubai, UAE: The Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) has granted conditional approval for a new indication of AstraZeneca’s Ultomiris® (ravulizumab) to reduce proteinuria in adults with primary immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) who are at risk of disease progression, making the UAE the first country in the world to approve this indication. Ultomiris® has been registered in the UAE since 2022 for the treatment of several rare diseases. 

The approval is in line with the UAE’s strategic priorities and the “We the UAE 2031” vision, which aims to strengthen the country’s leadership and global competitiveness in vital sectors, particularly healthcare and pharmaceuticals, while advancing innovation, research and development.

It also supports EDE’s strategic objectives of building an advanced, proactive pharmaceutical regulatory system based on efficiency, regulatory excellence and the highest international standards of quality, safety and efficacy, helping accelerate patient access to the latest treatments.

Primary IgA nephropathy is an immune-mediated kidney disease caused by the deposition of an immune protein in kidney tissue, which can lead to inflammation and a gradual decline in kidney function. Elevated protein levels in the urine are an important indicator associated with disease progression, highlighting the need for treatment options that help reduce these levels and limit the risk of progression.

Dr Ruqaya Al Bastaki, Acting Executive Director of the Medical Products Regulation Sector at the Emirates Drug Establishment, said: “EDE’s regulatory framework is built on rigorous scientific assessment, striking a delicate balance between keeping pace with pharmaceutical advances and ensuring compliance with the highest standards of safety, quality and efficacy. The approval demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach.”

“It also reflects the Establishment’s commitment to strengthening the pharmaceutical sector’s readiness to respond to scientific developments and emerging treatments, reinforcing the UAE’s position among the leading countries in pharmaceutical regulation.”

Meanwhile, Sameh El Fangary, Gulf Cluster President at AstraZeneca, noted that conditional approval of the new indication for Ultomiris® in the UAE is an important step towards expanding the treatment options available to patients.

El Fangary added: “We look forward to continuing our collaboration with our partners in the UAE to support access to this treatment for eligible patients, helping improve treatment outcomes and enhance the quality of care they receive.”

The Emirates Drug Establishment also emphasised the importance of early diagnosis, regular monitoring of kidney function and protein levels in the urine, and adherence to the treatment plan prescribed by a specialist physician to help monitor and manage the condition and reduce potential complications.
